subject: Nanotechnology
title: Nano Scaffolds for Tissue
description: A fast breakdown of Nano Scaffolds for Tissue for builders.

hook.text: Grow a new ear on a scaffold — nanofiber meshes mimic the extracellular matrix that cells need to organize.

buildup.text: Electrospun nanofiber scaffolds provide structure, porosity, and biochemical cues for cell attachment.

discovery.text: Fiber diameter and alignment guide how cells grow — aligned fibers produce aligned tissue like tendons.

twist.text: Cells cannot penetrate dense nanofiber mats — pore size must be large enough for cells to migrate through.

climax.text: Electrospun skin grafts and vascular grafts are in clinical trials — nano scaffolds building real organs.

punchline.text: A web of nanofibers tells cells where to grow — and they obey.

quiz.question: Why are nanofiber scaffolds useful for tissue engineering?
options: They replace the need for living cells entirely
They mimic the extracellular matrix, guiding cell attachment and organization
They deliver oxygen directly to growing tissues
